title: The School of Athens
caption:
THE GREATEST GATHERING IN HISTORY

What if the greatest minds in history had all walked into the same room?

Raphael painted them together. But can you recognize them?

slides.headline: Every genius in one room.
slides.alt: The vaulted hall of the School of Athens with the crowd of philosophers small on the steps below.
slides.caption:
THE GREATEST GATHERING IN HISTORY

What if the greatest minds in history had all walked into the same room?

Raphael painted them together. But can you recognize them?

slides.headline: Plato and Aristotle, you all know. But what about the rest?
slides.alt: Plato pointing upward with his Timaeus beside Aristotle holding his palm over the ground, Ethics under his arm. Numbered 01 of 08.
slides.caption:
TWO MEN. TWO WORLDS.

One points to the heavens. The other, to the earth.

Plato and Aristotle. Two different ways of understanding the universe.

slides.headline: Diogenes
slides.alt: Diogenes sprawled alone across the marble steps in a blue robe, reading a sheet. Numbered 02.
slides.caption:
THE MAN WHO REJECTED EVERYTHING

Diogenes. The philosopher who challenged wealth, power and social conventions.

slides.headline: Pythagoras
slides.alt: Pythagoras writing in a book on his knee while a boy holds a slate of musical ratios. Numbered 03.
slides.caption:
THE MATHEMATICIAN

Pythagoras. The man who saw the universe through numbers and mathematical harmony.

slides.headline: Euclid
slides.alt: Euclid, bald, bending over a slate with a compass as students crowd round. Numbered 04.
slides.caption:
THE MAN DRAWING ON THE FLOOR

Euclid. Geometry was his language, and the compass in his hand gives him away.

slides.headline: Heraclitus
slides.alt: Heraclitus sitting alone against a marble block, chin on his fist, writing. Numbered 05.
slides.caption:
THE LONELY THINKER

Heraclitus. Seated alone, absorbed in thought. His face is believed to be modeled after Michelangelo.

slides.headline: Zoroaster & Ptolemy
slides.alt: Bearded Zoroaster holding a starry sphere and crowned Ptolemy, seen from behind, holding a globe of the Earth. Numbered 06.
slides.caption:
THE TWO MEN HOLDING THE GLOBES

Ptolemy and Zoroaster. One holds the terrestrial globe, the other the celestial sphere.

slides.headline: Socrates
slides.alt: Socrates in an olive robe counting on his fingers to a young listener. Numbered 07.
slides.caption:
THE QUESTIONER

Socrates. Surrounded by listeners, doing what he did best: questioning everything.

slides.headline: Raphael
slides.alt: Raphael in a black cap at the far right, looking out at the viewer beside an older man in a white cap. Numbered 08.
slides.caption:
THE ARTIST HIDING IN HIS OWN PAINTING

Raphael included himself among the philosophers. Can you find him?

slides.headline: The School of Athens, mapped
slides.alt: The whole fresco in a gold frame with eight numbered gold discs on the figures, and a key listing their names.
slides.caption:
ONE PAINTING. AN ENTIRE WORLD OF IDEAS.

More than 500 years later, we're still discovering the people, ideas and stories hidden inside this masterpiece.

Which philosopher would you have wanted to meet?

notes: Captions are per slide (slides[].caption, the owner's text, verbatim); top-level caption = slide 1's. Slides 3-10 carry only the number and name. Who's-who style (new, 21 Nov 2026): one numbered figure per slide, full-bleed crops from the 17402 px Commons scan, numeral in the text block so it never covers a face, then a map numbering all eight. Slide 2 (Plato & Aristotle) doubles as the second hook. Old story version: archive/slides-story-v1.html (its images in img/archive/). Identifications are traditional; Euclid/Bramante and Heraclitus/Michelangelo hedged ('said to be', 'widely read as'); Zoroaster/Ptolemy hedged 'traditionally'. Raphael's self-portrait stated by the Vatican Museums. Map discs placed by eye on each figure's head.
